title: Diphthongs and Triphthongs
subtitle: When two or three vowels share one syllable.
objectives: Recognize falling diphthongs (ai, ei, oi, ui, au, eu).
Recognize rising diphthongs with semivowels (ia, ie, io, iu, ua, ue, ui, uo).
Pronounce triphthongs (iai, iei, uoi) as one syllable.
Distinguish diphthong from hiatus (two separate vowels).

sections.heading: What is a diphthong?
sections.body: A diphthong is two vowel sounds in one syllable. Italian has both falling diphthongs (stress on the first vowel, glide to the second) and rising diphthongs (glide from a semivowel to a full vowel). Falling: mai (never), sei (six), poi (then), lui (he), pausa (pause), Europa (Europe). Rising: piano (flat, slow), piede (foot), uomo (man), guanto (glove). A triphthong is three vowels in one syllable: miei (my, masculine plural), tuoi (your, masculine plural). Rare but grammatical.

sections.heading: Diphthong versus hiatus
sections.body: Not all vowel sequences form diphthongs. When two vowels are in separate syllables, that is hiatus. paura (fear): pa-U-ra (three syllables, hiatus between a and u); pausa (pause): PAU-sa (two syllables, diphthong au). poeta (poet): po-E-ta (three syllables, hiatus); piede (foot): PIE-de (two syllables, diphthong ie). Stress falls on the open vowel of a diphthong unless a written accent overrides.

sections.heading: From Petrarch
sections.body: Petrarch, Canzoniere 1: Voi ch'ascoltate in rime sparse il suono. rime: one syllable, ri-me? No: RI-me (two syllables). sparse: SPAR-se. suono: two syllables, suo-no? No: SUO-no (diphthong uo). Dante, Inferno I: Nel mezzo del cammin di nostra vita. mezzo: no diphthong, MED-dzo. cammin: cam-MIN. nostra: NO-stra. vita: VI-ta.

sections.heading: Listening drill
sections.instructions: Ten words with diphthongs and hiatus. Listen; repeat.

items.answer: Two vowel sounds in one syllable.

items.prompt: Is pausa a diphthong or hiatus?
Is paura a diphthong or hiatus?

items.answer: mai, sei, poi, lui — each a single syllable.
